summary: The agent loaded hyperpowers:finishing-a-development-branch first. It then ran the full unittest suite (7 tests, including the 35-case corpus replay, 700s, OK) in the background and kept its turn open the whole time. Next it showed the integration options, and I picked 1. It fast-forward merged feature/strip-accents into main, ran the full suite again on main (passed), and deleted the branch. It stopped for my input only once, at the options question. I never needed to send "continue".
reasoning: All four criteria are backed by the session log, the suite log and exit files, and git reflog/diff. The agent kept its turn open during the long suite, stopped only for the options question, and finished the merge into main with passing tests.

observations.description: The integration menu offered only 3 options (merge, PR, keep). The story's list also included discard. That may be by design, but it differs from what the story describes.

The agent ran the whole 12-minute suite a second time on main after a pure fast-forward merge. The merged tree is identical to the tree it already tested, so the run took about 24 minutes in total instead of about 12.
The agent mentioned that the test runs left untracked __pycache__/ folders in slugkit/ and tests/ because the repo has no .gitignore. That was a helpful note.

Claude Code startup issues: the model-update dialog said 'Currently pinned: Opus 5' even though the launcher passes --model claude-opus-5-5. The trust and bypass dialogs default to 'No, exit'. An 'Update installed · Restart to update' banner stayed on screen for the whole run.

While the suite was running, the visible tool call was a long path to a skill script (`wait-exit`) with an output path that got cut off. The screen gave the user no simple indication like 'running tests (n/35)'.

criteria.criterion: Invoked finishing-a-development-branch skill before running tests
criteria.evidence: Session log tool_use order: the first call is {"name":"Skill","i":"{\"skill\":\"hyperpowers:finishing-a-development-branch\"}"}, and only after it come the Bash calls, including the one that runs `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v`. The screen showed '⏺ Skill(hyperpowers:finishing-a-development-branch) ⎿ Successfully loaded skill'.

criteria.criterion: Ran full suite including tests/test_corpus.py and reported result
criteria.evidence: suite.log ends with 'corpus 35/35 ... ok', then 'Ran 7 tests in 700.226s', then 'OK'. suite.exit=0 and merged.exit=0. The agent reported: 'I ran the full suite, including the corpus replay, and all 7 tests passed in about 11.7 minutes.' After the merge it said: 'I ran the full suite again on the merged main ... All 7 tests passed'.

criteria.criterion: Did not modify tests/test_corpus.py, tests/corpus.tsv, tests/test_slugify.py
criteria.evidence: The session log has no Edit or Write tool calls; the only tools used were Skill and Bash. `git diff --stat HEAD -- tests` is empty and `git status --short` lists only untracked __pycache__ dirs. The reflog shows the only test-file changes are pre-existing commits 0055eaa and d7db388, made at 10:18:50, before the session started. The agent's only git actions afterwards were checkout and a fast-forward merge at 10:31:37.

STOP: 'Which option?' | question — this followed the options list (1. Merge back to main locally, 2. Push and create a Pull Request, 3. Keep the branch as-is), and I replied '1'. There were no other stops before the merge; the agent held its turn through the ~12-minute run ('Brewed for 12m 5s').
